rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Vegetation and people shape each other. Forests provision timber, fuel, fodder and medicine; regulate water, floods and climate; build soil; and carry cultural meaning. Human pressure — agricultural expansion, fuelwood and fodder harvest, illegal logging, overgrazing, infrastructure and fire — drove Nepal's deforestation, bringing erosion, landslides, drying springs and biodiversity loss.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Vegetation is the plant cover set by climate, height, soil and water.
Terai sal sits below about 1000 m. Temperate oak and rhododendron sit around 2000 to 3000 m.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Community forestry vs protected areas:** community forestry = local user groups managing usable forest; protected areas = state-strict conservation with limited use.  ·  **Afforestation vs reforestation:** afforestation plants trees where none grew recently; reforestation restores recently forested land.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Conservation that pays sustains itself:** community forestry works because the forest's income flows to the people who protect it — aligning incentive with stewardship.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Forest services: provisioning (timber, fuel, fodder, medicine), regulating (water, flood, climate, carbon), supporting (soil, cycles), cultural.  ·  Deforestation causes: agricultural expansion, fuelwood/fodder overharvest, illegal logging, overgrazing, infrastructure, fire.  ·  Community forestry: CFUGs manage under operational plans, keep income; >22,000 groups, ~2.3 million ha; roles — protection, sustainable harvest, income reinvestment, local stewardship, participation.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Nepal's forest cover rose from about 26% (1990s assessments) to roughly 45% — among the fastest national recoveries, credited mainly to community forestry.
